text:
A: Hi. Erm, can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Graham.
A: I'm Sana. Sorry, I'm quite tired now. I thought the last one was the end.
B: Ar. Me an' all.
A: Where are you?
B: Tipton. Black Country.
A: I'm in Luton. Erm, I saw the photo behind you. Is that your grandchildren?
B: Yeah. Our son's two. They come Sundays.
A: Aw. How old are they?
B: Seven and nine. And our daughter's lad, he's four.
A: Oh, my son's five. Zayan. He'd probably get on with the four-year-old. Is he into dinosaurs?
B: Diggers. Tractors. Anything with an engine.
A: Ha, that's nice. Zayan just roars at everyone. He's got this green T-rex, he takes it everywhere. He took it to school and it went missing for a whole day, he was in bits.
B: Did they find it?
A: In the lost property, yeah. I think the teacher felt sorry for him.
B: Good.
A: Erm, do you do things with them? Like, on Sundays?
B: Fix their bikes, mostly. The lad helps me in the shed. Hands me the wrong spanner.
A: Aw, that's sweet. Zayan's just learning to ride his bike, but the chain keeps coming off and I don't know what I'm doing. I just kind of push it back on and hope.
B: Ar, that's it really. Back wheel might want pulling back. Tightening. If it keeps coming off.
A: Pulling the wheel back? Okay. I'll ask my brother. He'll pretend he knows.
B: Most do.
A: Ha! Erm, what did you do, sorry, for work?
B: Toolmaker. Retired now. Three year.
A: Do you like being retired?
B: Er... it's quiet. I feed the birds. Shed. Grandkids Sunday.
A: That sounds kind of nice though. I'd love quiet. I work in a school kitchen, it's never quiet.
B: No. Wouldn't be.
A: Sorry, I don't know if I'm asking the right things.
B: Yow're doing fine.
A: Thank you. I think that's nearly time.
B: Ar. Hope he gets the bike going.
A: Me too. It was nice to meet you, Graham.
B: Tara.
